subject: PayGrid model fit eval — parity thresholds & next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@paygrid.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 15:15:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap: model fit eval & next steps

Hi Sofia / Tom — great to speak earlier. Quick recap and action items from today's discovery / eval sync: 

1) Goal: Confirm whether open models can reach parity with PayGrid's proprietary baseline on intent classification + entity extraction for payments flows. Your success criteria were: parity within ~3% of baseline on macro-F1 and no regression on high-risk intents.

2) Data & scope: We agreed on a 5k example eval set covering live traffic slices (auth failures, refunds, payouts, KYC-related flows). You mentioned pulling a redacted sample and a representative prompt set — thanks.

3) Recommended models to start with (initial shortlist):
   - Mistral-Instruct-7B (open) — strong instruction-following, fast inference
   - Llama 3 70B (quantized variant) — higher-capacity baseline for tougher prompts
   - Redmond-proprietary (your existing baseline) — used for parity comparison

4) Metrics & acceptance thresholds:
   - Macro-F1 parity target: within 3% of baseline
   - High-risk intents (payments declines / fraud flags): 95% recall minimum
   - Latency: 95th percentile under 300ms for key routes (for dedicated infra later)

5) Next steps we agreed on:
   - PayGrid: share the redacted 5k eval set + example prompts (Sofia) — by EOD Tuesday
   - Redwood: run A/B eval across the shortlisted open models vs your baseline; deliver benchmark CSV + recommended prompt tuning and temperature settings (Lauren / Marissa) — within 3 business days after we get the data
   - Alignment call: quick results review and roll decision meeting (30m) — propose Thu next week

Attachments referenced: paygrid_benchmark_results.csv (we'll upload initial template once we run the job) and open-model-prompt-set.jsonl (we'll share our starter prompt set).

Please reply if I missed anything. Happy to adjust timelines if you need more time to redact.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

From: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@paygrid.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@paygrid.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 16:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit eval & next steps

Thanks Lauren — this looks correct, appreciate the clear recap. A couple of clarifications: 

- We'll send the redacted 5k set tomorrow morning (we're running a final PII scrub). Expect a CSV with intent labels + span annotations for entity extraction.
- For the high-risk intents, we should also include a small set of flagged examples (approx 200) where previous models underperformed — will include a column called "priority_risk" so you can weight them in the evaluation.

I'm attaching a short CSV sample (sample_eval_schema.csv) so you can confirm the format.

Also: can you confirm whether the Mistral-Instruct-7B run will be done as-is or with light instruction fine-tuning / prompt templating? We want to understand how much prompt engineering vs model-size improvement matters for parity.

Sofia Martinez
Head of ML Ops | PayGrid
sofia.martinez@paygrid.com

Attachment: sample_eval_schema.csv (CSV, 12 KB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@paygrid.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit eval & next steps

Thanks Sofia — perfect. We reviewed your sample schema and it looks good. Quick answers and plan: 

- Mistral-Instruct-7B: we'll run three variants in the eval: out-of-the-box (zero-shot), prompt-templated (few-shot templates + system instruction), and light instruction-tuning (1-2 epoch lora on a 2k subset if needed). That will help isolate gains from prompt engineering vs model capacity.
- Llama 3 70B: we'll run a quantized inferencing path (float16 / 4-bit quantization where possible) with the templated prompts. Expect higher baseline quality but higher cost and latency.

What we'll deliver after the run (timeline: 72 hours after we receive your redacted data):
- paygrid_benchmark_results.csv: per-example outputs and metrics (accuracy, macro-F1, recall by intent bucket)
- open-model-prompt-set.jsonl: the prompts + instruction templates we used for reproducibility
- short write-up: recommended model + configuration and notes on any quality regressions (if observed)

Acceptance / parity framing (proposal):
- Primary: Macro-F1 within 3% of your baseline across the 5k set
- Secondary: No more than 2% absolute drop on the high-risk intent recall bucket; otherwise we classify as regression and flag for either additional tuning or fallback routing to baseline

We will also include a column in the CSV with confidence scores so you can evaluate calibration differences.

Proposed review slot: Thu 18 Mar, 10:00–10:30 PT (I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm).

Attachments we will include in the drop: paygrid_benchmark_results.csv, open-model-prompt-set.jsonl.

Cheers,
Lauren
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: Exec prep + eval run plan (PayGrid)

Lauren / Aditya — looping internal next steps and owner items before the run: 

- Aditya: please provision the evaluation jobs on our staging infra (Mistral-7B, Llama3-70B quant path). Use the workload profile from the schema and ensure we capture latency at 50/95/99 percentiles. ETA: Wed EOD for run completion.
- Lauren: I'll draft the short write-up and parity table templates; will include the acceptance thresholds you outlined (3% macro-F1 / 95% recall high-risk).
- Add a regression flag flow: if we see >2% absolute drop on high-risk intents, mark as regression and include suggestions: prompt tuning, LoRA, or fallback to proprietary route for those intents.

I'll coordinate with SRE to ensure KV cache warm-up for the Llama runs so the latency numbers are representative. Also note: include cost estimate per 1M inference tokens for each model option in the write-up — that'll matter for Tom & procurement.

I'll notify Lauren when the initial CSV/JSONL artifacts are uploaded to the drive link.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
